newsitem.title: THAILAND: Future of Thai zero-tariff corn import uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Future of Thai zero-tariff corn import uncertain.

text.p: The Thai government has not yet decided when 200,000 tonnes of corn can be imported under the zero-tariff programme, as local price conditions have not been met, a commerce ministry official said on Friday.

Siriphol Yodmaungchareon, deputy director general for Internal Trade Department, told Reuters that the government allowed the imports only if the average price of domestic corn between March 11-31 was 4.50 baht ($0.17) per kg.
"So far it has not reached that level yet ... the average price during that period stood around 4.40-4.45 baht a kg," he said.
But the official declined to say if the condition will be modified.

The feed industry expected the government to come up with the import schedule soon as the deadline for imports to arrive in Thailand is June 30, with local supplies due to come onto the market in July.
South America is the most economically viable origin for corn right now and shipments from South America take more than a month to arrive.
Trade sources said the feed industry might opt for imports under the World Trade Organization rule which allows 52,000 tonnes to be imported for a 20-percent tariff.
"My hunch is there might not be any zero-tariff imports this year," said one Bangkok-based trader.
In March Thailand approved a commerce ministry proposal to allow a zero-tariff corn import quota of 200,000 tonnes by July 1997. ($1 = 26 baht)
